meta.purpose: A review queue. Nothing on this list is implemented except where status says so. Each item states what it would change, what it costs, what evidence it needs, and what would have to be true before it is safe to ship. Suggestions SUG-19 to SUG-29 were added by the integration pass and cover design polish, editorial cadence, organic-traffic prerequisites and the two things this site must never build.

scoring_legend.impact: 1 = cosmetic, 5 = changes whether a reader buys or whether the site can earn at all
scoring_legend.effort: 1 = under an hour, 5 = multi-week or needs an account this session does not hold
scoring_legend.confidence: how sure we are that the effect is real, not how much we like the idea. 'no data' means we are guessing.

meta.read_this_first: Rows marked shipped are already live. Rows marked blocked are not a to-do list for a future agent; they are things only the account owner can unblock.

suggestions.title: Publish the disclosure in a strip under the masthead, and again in the footer
suggestions.why: Both Amazon's Operating Agreement and the FTC's guidance put the duty on the publisher, and the FTC's test is whether a reader can weigh the recommendation at the moment they read it. A disclosure only in the footer fails that test on a long page.
suggestions.confidence: high — it is a stated obligation, not a hypothesis
suggestions.evidence_needed: none; the sources are already read and quoted
suggestions.shipped_note: Present on every page, generated by one template, so a new page cannot ship without it.

suggestions.title: Stop publishing prices, star ratings and review counts entirely
suggestions.why: Program Policies 2(b) allows price display only when Amazon serves the link carrying the data, or when it comes from the Creators API / PA API. This site has no such feed. A stale price is also a misrepresentation risk under the same section.
suggestions.evidence_needed: none
suggestions.shipped_note: No number appears on any product surface. The blank is deliberate and is explained in-line, not hidden.

suggestions.title: Keep intended ASIN and observed redirect target as two separate, never-merged fields
suggestions.why: The observed redirect is a fact about today's redirect. The intended ASIN is a fact about what the owner meant to enrol. Merging them destroys the only audit trail that would catch a wrong-product redirect.
suggestions.evidence_needed: none
suggestions.shipped_note: products.json carries them in separate keys. intended_asin is deliberately null for all five rows.

suggestions.title: Build the landing page as a publication front page, with the audit surfaces demoted to the footer
suggestions.why: A buyer arriving from a search result needs a reason to stay within about five seconds. A verification table is a reason to leave. The register still has to exist; it just should not be the front door.
suggestions.confidence: medium — standard practice, not measured on this site
suggestions.evidence_needed: post-launch: scroll depth and outbound click rate by page
suggestions.shipped_note: Front page leads with the products and the guides. Every register is reachable from the footer.

suggestions.title: Write question-shaped guides, one per real buyer decision, and link products from inside the argument
suggestions.why: A guide that answers a question earns a link and a share; a product card does not. Question-shaped titles also match how people type into a search box.
suggestions.confidence: medium — the titles are hypotheses until query data exists
suggestions.evidence_needed: Search Console query data after 4–6 weeks
suggestions.shipped_note: Four guides published. Every claim inside them is either quoted from a listing title or omitted.

suggestions.title: Ship an RSS feed and one canonical host, before chasing traffic
suggestions.why: Syndication gives a second surface for free and makes the publishing cadence visible. Duplicate hosts split whatever authority the site earns.
suggestions.confidence: high on the mechanics, medium on the size of the effect
suggestions.evidence_needed: none for the mechanics
suggestions.shipped_note: feed.xml plus rel=alternate on every page, canonical tags throughout, robots.txt pointing at the sitemap.

suggestions.title: Define the five events and a privacy-preserving outbound-click counter — but deploy nothing until a host is chosen
suggestions.why: Measurement has to exist before optimisation, or the next decision is made on instinct. But an unhosted endpoint and an unconsented cookie are worse than no measurement: one is dead code, the other is a compliance problem.
suggestions.confidence: high on the event schema, n/a on the effect until data exists
suggestions.evidence_needed: a first-party host (see FLG-009)
suggestions.blocked_note: The schema is published in events.json. The collector is a documented design, not live code. No third-party script is loaded on this site.

suggestions.title: Test exactly one Special Link end to end before scaling to five
suggestions.why: If the tag is dropping, one wrong link and five wrong links cost the same in lost trust but five is a bigger hole. One-link-per-product, confirmed in the Associates report, is the cheapest possible experiment.
suggestions.confidence: high — this is the owner's own stated plan, and it is the right one
suggestions.evidence_needed: an Associates dashboard session
suggestions.blocked_note: Requires reading the click report in the Associates dashboard. This session has no account access.

suggestions.title: Add a comparison table that compares on decisions, not on specs we cannot verify
suggestions.why: A reader choosing between a dual basket and a French-door oven wants to know which one their counter and their family size can actually accommodate. That comparison is honest without needing a wattage figure we cannot source.
suggestions.evidence_needed: none for the form-factor comparison; dimensions would need a feed
suggestions.shipped_note: The compare page compares form factor, what the seller claims, and what to check in person. It does not invent a winner.

suggestions.title: Publish a 'Flagged for Review' page and keep it visible in the footer
suggestions.why: Every unverified value has to be reviewable by the person who can actually resolve it. A hidden to-do list gets ignored; a public page with source links gets acted on.
suggestions.evidence_needed: none
suggestions.shipped_note: /flagged/ lists every irregularity with its source link.

suggestions.title: Add author identity and a methodology page before adding more content
suggestions.why: Readers and search engines both discount anonymous product advice. An author page with a real name, a stated method and a correction policy is the cheapest credibility upgrade available.
suggestions.evidence_needed: a real name and a real bio from the owner
suggestions.blocked_note: A method page exists. An author page does not, because inventing a persona would be exactly the failure mode this project is trying to avoid.

suggestions.title: Publish one guide every two weeks rather than five at once
suggestions.why: A cadence is a signal that the site is maintained. A burst followed by silence reads as abandoned, and it also makes it impossible to attribute a change in traffic to a topic.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Search Console data to confirm the cadence is producing indexed pages
suggestions.blocked_note: No new guides should be drafted until SUG-08 resolves, so that the first guide is measured against a working link.

suggestions.title: Add a reader-capture email list
suggestions.why: An email list is the only audience asset that survives an algorithm change. It is also the highest-risk item on this list, because it brings CAN-SPAM, consent records and a provider into scope at once.
suggestions.evidence_needed: a provider, a privacy review, and an unsubscribe path
suggestions.blocked_note: Not built. A signup box that silently does nothing is worse than no signup box.

suggestions.title: Connect the Creators API or PA API and serve live price and availability
suggestions.why: This is the only route that makes a price legal to display, and price is the single most-requested datum on a buying page. It also unlocks real availability, which prevents sending readers to an out-of-stock listing.
suggestions.confidence: high on the value, high on the constraint
suggestions.evidence_needed: Associates account approval plus API credentials
suggestions.blocked_note: Until then the correct behaviour is to show no price. Do not fill this gap with a scrape.

suggestions.title: Add structured data for articles and breadcrumbs
suggestions.why: Article and BreadcrumbList markup help a search engine describe the page correctly. Product and Offer markup is deliberately excluded, because marking up an offer implies price and availability data this site does not have.
suggestions.evidence_needed: rich-result eligibility check after indexing
suggestions.shipped_note: Article and BreadcrumbList only. No Product, no Offer, no AggregateRating.

suggestions.title: Add a visual product gallery with Amazon-hosted imagery
suggestions.why: Images carry a buyer further than paragraphs. But Program Content may not be altered, and an image cannot be used in a way that implies an endorsement.
suggestions.evidence_needed: a compliant image route: Amazon-served widgets, or the API's image fields used unmodified
suggestions.blocked_note: Rejected for now rather than approximated with stock photography, which would misrepresent the product. See FLG-015.

suggestions.title: Publish a per-guide 'what we could not verify' box
suggestions.why: Stating the limits next to the recommendation is what separates a publication from an advertorial, and it costs one component.
suggestions.evidence_needed: none
suggestions.shipped_note: Each guide closes with a 'What this guide does not claim' block.

suggestions.title: Run paid search to accelerate
suggestions.why: It is the fastest way to buy traffic.
suggestions.confidence: high that it is the wrong move
suggestions.evidence_needed: n/a
suggestions.blocked_note: Purchases arriving through paid search, and through search-engine or redirecting links generally, are disqualified under the Commission Income Statement, and bidding on Amazon marks is separately prohibited. Paid search would spend money to generate non-commissionable orders. See S07.

suggestions.title: Finish the illustration system so every guide opens with a real image
suggestions.why: A text-only page is the single most common tell of a generated site. Five hand-commissioned-style illustrations now run on the front page, but seven of the nine guides still open with text. Consistent artwork is also the difference between a page a reader screenshots and shares and one they do not, and it is what makes a card legible in a search result or a feed reader.
suggestions.confidence: medium — it improves the perceived quality and click-through of a page; it does not by itself earn a ranking
suggestions.evidence_needed: One art direction decision (palette and composition are already fixed in assets/css/site.css), then ~15 minutes per remaining guide.
suggestions.note: Illustrations are made for this publication and captioned as such. They must never be swapped for Amazon listing photos: see SUG-25.

suggestions.title: Rotate a seasonal shelf by date, not by rebuild
suggestions.why: Kitchen-gear intent is seasonal: Thanksgiving and holiday hosting now, party appetisers in December, meal-prep in January, grill-adjacent gear in May. A shelf that swaps with the calendar keeps the front page current without touching the data layer, and it puts the right question in front of the right month.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Decide whether a static build (re-run tools/build.py on a schedule) or a small client-side date check is acceptable. If the front page must be identical for every visitor — which is what a crawler sees — the build must re-run, not the browser.
suggestions.note: The first seasonal feature is live now (the holiday overflow guide). What is not built is the rotation.

suggestions.title: Build hub pages around situations, not superlatives
suggestions.why: “Best air fryer 2026” is the query with volume, and it is the one this site cannot answer honestly: ranking products requires either hands-on testing we have not done or third-party scores we are not licensed to republish. A hub page for “a small kitchen that cooks for two” or “one that has to fit a sheet pan” can be answered from listing facts, is the same search intent, and is defensible line by line.
suggestions.confidence: high that it is the only compliant version of the idea; medium on traffic
suggestions.evidence_needed: Two or three hubs, each assembled from fields already in src/data/products.json, plus one sentence per claim naming its source.

suggestions.title: Verify Search Console and Bing Webmaster on the day the site is live
suggestions.why: Nothing else on this board can be decided with evidence until queries arrive. Search Console is the only source that tells us which questions people actually came in asking, which is the input the editorial queue is supposed to be re-ordered by. Until a property is verified, the queue on /topics/ is reasoning, not measurement.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Account access this session does not have and should not fake: property verification is done by the person who owns the domain and the GitHub organisation.
suggestions.blocked_note: No site-verification record, token or meta tag was added by an agent, because a verified property implies an owner who agreed to it. The sitemap and robots file are already published and correct, so verification is the only missing step.

suggestions.title: Give every guide a FAQ block with matching structured data
suggestions.why: Question-shaped guides already read like answers; marking them up lets a search engine see the question and the answer as a pair. Five new guides ship with it today. The four earlier guides have the questions in prose but no markup, so the set is inconsistent.
suggestions.confidence: medium — markup is a comprehension aid, not a ranking promise
suggestions.evidence_needed: Move each guide's closing question list into the existing FAQ schema shape. Do not write questions a reader did not ask.

suggestions.title: Weekly automated audit of links, disclosure and claims
suggestions.why: The compliance state of this site is only true for the hour it was built. A listing disappears, a redirect changes, a page ships without the disclosure strip — and the site is silently non-compliant. tools/validate.py already checks all of that in a single pass; running it weekly converts a one-off good state into an ongoing one.
suggestions.evidence_needed: A scheduled workflow running build + validate and opening an issue on failure. No secrets needed; no data leaves the repository.
suggestions.note: Amazon's link behaviour also drifts: one supplied link resolved for two sessions and returned a bot interstitial for a third. A weekly check is the only way to notice without someone remembering to look.
suggestions.shipped_note: Both halves are in the repository now: .github/workflows/pages.yml rebuilds from the data layer and runs tools/validate.py before publishing anything, and weekly-audit.yml re-runs the same gate on a schedule without deploying. What is deliberately not automated: watching Amazon's own pages, which no script in this repository should be doing.

suggestions.title: Do not display Amazon listing images, copy listing descriptions, or republish ratings
suggestions.why: Program Content — images, descriptions, ratings and review text — may be used only as provided through Amazon's own linking tools or the Product Advertising / Creators API, and ratings and customer reviews only when obtained through that API. Hand-copied screenshots and pasted bullet points are the most common cause of an account closing, and the risk is highest on a site that looks like it has a feed but does not.
suggestions.confidence: high — it is a stated restriction, not a judgement call
suggestions.evidence_needed: Nothing. This is a prohibition to observe, recorded here so the next session does not ‘improve’ the product cards by scraping.
suggestions.note: Rejected means: do not build it. If API access is ever granted, the replacement is a live pull with a date and time stamp beside the price, not a static copy.

suggestions.title: Do not build price history, price-drop alerts or a comparison engine
suggestions.why: The Participation Requirements state that, unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, an Associate site must not have price-tracking or price-alerting functionality. A price-alert feature is the standard affiliate playbook and the standard account-closing move. The FTC's concern points the same way: an alert that goes out with stale numbers is a misleading claim sent to someone who trusted you.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Nothing; the restriction is published. Recorded so the absence of price data reads as a policy decision and not an oversight.
suggestions.note: Rejected means: this is not on the roadmap. Every blank price cell on the site is the visible consequence of obeying it.

suggestions.title: Turn the ledger into an importer, with the report as the only input
suggestions.why: The campaign ledger is empty by design and must stay that way until numbers arrive from the enrolled account's own reports. The safe automation is a one-way importer that reads an exported report, appends rows with a timestamp and a provenance field, and refuses to compute anything not present in the file.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Report access, plus an agreed export format. Never scrape the dashboard into a database — that is a separate restriction and an unnecessary risk.
suggestions.blocked_note: No authorized report has ever been read. Any session that fills this table before then is fabricating data, which is why the empty state is published rather than removed.

suggestions.title: Name a human editor, with a bio that survives an audit
suggestions.why: E-E-A-T is not a ranking factor you can install, but a publication with no named person behind it is indistinguishable from a content farm to both a reader and a quality rater. The byline currently says ‘editorial desk’ on purpose: inventing a person who has tested products would be a fabricated endorsement, which is exactly what the FTC's guides prohibit.
suggestions.evidence_needed: One real person who agrees to be named, two true sentences about what they have actually done, and a corrections record they own.
suggestions.blocked_note: Only the site owner can supply this. Until then /about/#who says the byline is a desk, and the site claims no testing.

suggestions.title: Publish a downloadable capacity worksheet as the linkable asset
suggestions.why: Guides get read; assets get linked. A one-page worksheet — measure your pan, count your one-layer portions, list the three dishes that would move off your oven — is genuinely useful, costs nothing to maintain, and is the kind of thing a niche newsletter or forum answer cites. It also sends readers back to the register with a question they can now answer.
suggestions.confidence: medium — outreach-driven, and the effect is not measurable until Search Console is verified
suggestions.evidence_needed: A print-ready PDF generated from the same data as the capacity guide, and a decision about whether to accept links at all (no paid links, no guest-post farms).

suggestions.title: Hold every tracking tag behind a data-file gate until enrolment is confirmed
suggestions.why: Publishing a tag asserts a relationship: that this site is listed on an enrolled Associates account for that ID. Nothing in the repository can confirm it, and a link that is unregistered or improperly formatted is the publisher's breach — Operating Agreement §2 lets Amazon withhold commission for a violation, while the Commission Income Statement already disqualifies purchases arriving through an untagged redirect. So the safe launch state is disclosed reference links, and monetization becomes a data edit rather than a claim.
suggestions.confidence: high — it is a stated condition of the program, and the flip is one file
suggestions.evidence_needed: the owner's own confirmation in Associates Central, then one observed click in the report
suggestions.shipped_note: tools/build.py reads src/data/product-intent.json; tools/validate.py fails the build if a tag appears while the gate flags are false; tools/arm_links.py refuses to arm the site without --i-am-the-owner.
